en: The Eight Auspicious Verses:
Mañjuśrī, the Lord of the World; the Victorious One’s supreme crown; Jambhala; Vajrasattva; Maitreya; Vajrapāṇi; the lotus that brings happiness; Rāhula; and Bhadrapāla.

May the Buddha Vairocana and the others, who are revered by the three worlds and whose faults are entirely exhausted, and may the Bodhisattvas, who are of equal flavor and well-pleased, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. (1)
The joyful Hūṃkāravajra, the subduer of Paśupati, and the joyful Vajraghaṇṭā; the yellow Hālāhalāsya, the destroyer of hosts of enemies, the great-souled Ṭakkirāja;
Akṣobhya, Ratnaketu, Acala, Gaṇḍahasti, and Yamāri—[these appear] every day.
May the Bodhisattvas, being praised and being of one flavor with the ultimate reality, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. || 2 ||
The Saṃgha is the kinsman of the three worlds, the abode of a multitude of virtues, the mind of awakening, and the pure mind;
awakening is the accomplishment of bliss, having conquered the impurities of the Kali age; Heruka is the Blue Staff;
the Buddha is the King of the Deer, who has conquered the qualities of the Victors and is compassionate toward all sentient beings.
May the Bodhisattvas, who are of equal flavor with the Dharma, being satisfied, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. || 3 ||
Prajñā, who has descended as Candra; her younger sister Bhṛkuṭī, who bears the burden of the equipment of gnosis (jñānasaṃbhāra);
Mārīcī, the slayer of Māra, who removes all fears and is yellow in color with three faces; Māyūrī and Māmakī, who have destroyed the host of enemies; Pāṇḍarā, Rocanā, and the others—
May the Bodhisattvas, being praised and being of one taste with the Dharma, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. (4)

Gāndhārī and Jāṅgulī, with hoods drawn back from her arms; Vārāhī, fierce with sword, noose, and goad, holding a vajra in her hand; Dharmadhātvīśvarī, bearing a sword and an axe; Keyūrī, the essence of gnosis, with a banner placed in her hand, possessing six arms, and Śābarī.
May the Bodhisattvas, who are of equal flavor with the ultimate reality, being satisfied, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. || 5 ||
Vaiṇyā, Mālyā, Sugītā, Śābarī renowned among the supreme Jinas, Dhūpavajrā, Vaitālī, Gandhavajrā, Prahasitavadanā, Svargati, Noble Tārā, Lakṣmī,
the Awakening of the Buddha, the remover of all fears, Śāradā, and Dīpavajrā.
May the Bodhisattvas, who are of equal flavor [with all beings], being satisfied, grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. || 6 ||
In Vaiśālī, on the mountain Gṛdhrakūṭa where his own power is renowned as the Wheel of Dharma,

in Śrāvastī, at Lumbinī where his hand was placed upon the earth, and at the Bodhi tree in Koṅkaṇa; [he bears] the Śrīvatsa, the leaf of the Aśvattha tree saluted by the best of gods, the Śrīphala fruit, the conch, and the wheel.
May the Bodhisattvas, being satisfied and of equal flavor [with all beings], grant the accomplishment of all aims and auspiciousness. (7)
An umbrella, dūrvā grass, a lotus, and a banner; gold, a fish, a tortoise, a boar, a full vase, the words of the best of sages, and the resonance of a vajra-bell.

May the Bodhisattvas, who possess the miraculous power of the Buddhas, who are bowed to by the best of gods, and who delight in the playful grace of laughter and dance—being of equal flavor with all things—grant the fulfillment of all aims and auspiciousness. 8.
The Maṅgalāṣṭaka is completed.
